_about: Cheat sheet of each policymaker's stated rate views, for the Summary on the dashboard's CB commentary page. Written by the scheduled labelling task (and by hand); keyed 'Bank|Name' as in speakers.json. Only what the person has actually said, paraphrased; leave a field empty rather than guess. Fields: votes {year: true/false} for yearly rotations (Fed), or {"YYYY-MM-DD": true/false} per meeting where the vote rotates meeting by meeting (ECB governors) - a meeting date wins over a year; stance hawk|lean hawk|centre|lean dove|dove (their own rate view, not market impact); next / following {call, note} for the next two rate-setting meetings - call is one of '+50', '+25 or +50', '+25', 'hike' (wants a hike, size not said), 'hold or +25', 'hold', '-25', 'open', '' (no view given); how = 'said' (they named this meeting or the move), 'implied' (follows from what they said, e.g. 'more hikes soon' or 'at least two more', without naming the meeting), or 'vote' (from their latest vote or minutes explanation); path {total, by, note} = the total move they want from here and by when, if they said; view = 1-2 sentences on their view of rates now; shift = how their view has changed recently; last = date of their last remark on rates (YYYY-MM-DD), ev = where; basis verbatim|reports; conf high|medium|low = how clearly they have said it; asof = when this entry was last reviewed.

Fed.note: Votes: 2026 = governors, Williams, Hammack, Logan, Kashkari, Paulson. From January 2027 the rotating seats pass to Goolsbee (Chicago), Barkin (Richmond), Daly (San Francisco) and the Atlanta Fed president (interim: Cheryl Venable). Oct 28 hold was 10-2, Cook and Hammack dissenting for a 25bp hike. Warsh gives no forward guidance.

ECB.note: The six Executive Board members always vote; national governors rotate monthly. Not voting in December: Netherlands (Sleijpen), Belgium (Wunsch), Bulgaria, Slovenia (Dolenc), Slovakia and Finland (Rehn). The 2027 rotation is not published yet, so February counts the Executive Board only. Lagarde announced on Oct 29 that she is leaving early (in February). Held at 2.50% on Oct 29 after hiking in September.

BoE.note: All nine MPC members vote at every meeting. Nov 5: hiked to 4.00% by 8-1, Mann voting for 50bp. Views below lean on each member's own explanation in the November minutes plus later remarks.

BoC.note: The Governing Council decides by consensus and publishes no individual votes, so everyone counts as deciding. Hiked to 2.50% on Oct 28; the summary of deliberations said further hikes may be needed. Macklem will not seek a second term (ends June 2027).

SNB.note: The three-member Governing Board decides by consensus at quarterly assessments. Policy rate 0%; the SNB says it would intervene in FX or even return to negative rates if needed, though the bar is higher.

next.note: Gives no forward guidance; did not push back on December hike pricing at the Oct 28 press conference.

path.note: Won't pre-judge meetings; calls the 2% goal a hard target.

Fed|Warsh.view: Inflation elevated and broadening, growth strong; framed the October hold as a pause to gather information, not a pivot.
Fed|Warsh.shift: Nov 16 speech on AI said nothing on rates.

next.note: Inflation will set his next move; adjustments decided by careful reading of the data. No size or timing given.

Fed|Jefferson.view: Inflation, not jobs, is the main signal for policy; PCE inflation still 3.6%, energy the main channel; upbeat on growth.
Fed|Jefferson.ev: Speech, UC San Diego Economic Roundtable

next.note: Not committed: will look at October PCE and November payrolls first; wants more information on the effect of the September hike.

path.note: Expects core PCE (about 3.3%) to move closer to 2% next year; financial conditions have tightened, so the costs of further tightening must be weighed.

Fed|Bowman.view: Still work to do on inflation, but leans toward patience; will look through temporary energy effects.
Fed|Bowman.shift: Oct 14: no urgency, time to wait and see. Unchanged in substance.

next.note: Nov 18: the Fed should hike 50bp in December, or else hike 25bp and signal faster increases; says a 'shock' may be needed. (Nov 10: 25bp base case, 50bp if October core CPI ran hot - it did.)

following.note: Not named. Implied by wanting faster hikes and 75-100bp or more in total.

path.note: Take back the three 2025 'insurance' cuts (75bp), maybe more; rates may need to rise 100bp or more.

Fed|Waller.view: Inflation is broadening and risks settling near 3%; the Fed needs to get more aggressive, and hiking only 25bp risks its credibility.
Fed|Waller.shift: More hawkish: from '25bp, 50 if CPI hot' (Nov 10) to pushing for 50bp (Nov 18).

next.note: Dissented on Oct 28 for a 25bp hike; no rate remarks since.

Fed|Cook.view: Only signal is her October dissent for a hike. Her recent news is the White House removal hearing (set for Dec 14), which she will not attend on its current terms.

next.note: No view given on December.

path.note: Sep 29: further rate hikes likely to be needed.

Fed|Barr.view: Recent speeches (Nov 12-16) were on AI, inequality and financial stability; said AI's impact so far shows up mostly in prices.

next.note: No public remarks on policy in the feed since stepping down as Chair; still a governor and a voter.
Ruled out a jumbo (50bp) move for December and says more hikes are likely needed, implying 25bp.

path.note: Said the AI boom could lead to more hikes in 2027.

Fed|Williams.view: Inflation too high and not moving in the right direction; economy getting stronger; recent gradual steps are working.
Fed|Williams.shift: More hawkish: Oct 13 saw no 2027 hike and Nov 6 wanted to gather more data; now sees more hikes likely, possibly into 2027.

next.note: Says more hikes are needed in small, steady 25bp steps and dissented for a hike in October; has not named December.

following.note: 'Gradual' read (by investingLive) as a hike every meeting; she flags bigger moves could become necessary.

path.note: Policy must move to restrictive; unclear how far the Fed has to go; the economy can handle more restriction.

Fed|Hammack.view: The Fed has missed on inflation for years and inflation is heading the wrong way; wants steady hikes into restrictive territory.

next.note: At least two more 25bp hikes needed, possibly faster this winter (Nov 10); December not named.

following.note: The second of the 'at least two' hikes, if they come back to back; not named.

path.note: Aim is a modestly restrictive stance; worried October PCE shows the same pickup as CPI.

Fed|Logan.view: Excess inflation is unacceptable; policy needs to get to modestly restrictive, more quickly if the data stay hot.
Fed|Logan.shift: More hawkish on pace: Oct 30 preferred a gradual pace; Nov 10 said hikes could come faster this winter.

next.note: Pencilled in one more hike in 2026 (late September); December is the only meeting left.

path.note: One more hike in 2026 and another in 2027; neutral rate may be higher than thought.

Fed|Kashkari.view: Inflation too high at about 3%, across the economy and not just energy; economy resilient. No rate remarks in the last six weeks.

next.note: Further gradual tightening 'seems appropriate'; no meeting or size named.

following.note: Gradual; would move faster if expectations, wages or underlying inflation rise. No meeting named.

path.note: Policy needs to be somewhat restrictive; puts underlying inflation at 2.5-3%.

Fed|Paulson.view: October CPI shows inflation pressures are still very much with us; more work to do.
Fed|Paulson.shift: Was among the doves on the tracker; now backs gradual hikes.

next.note: Wants more tightening and says hikes may need to be aggressive up front, but declined to prejudge size or timing.

following.note: Not prejudging; stubborn inflation could force more aggressive hikes.

path.note: Fed is not on a path back to 2% and must re-establish credibility.

Fed|Goolsbee.view: October CPI 'borderline disturbing'; AI data-centre boom looks like old-fashioned demand overheating.
Fed|Goolsbee.shift: Moved from centre to hawk through October-November.

next.note: No base case for December.

path.note: Direction is clear (higher), pace is the question; policy around or slightly below neutral.

Fed|Barkin.view: Inflation is the greatest risk, with broad-based cost pressures, but the Fed should move with care.

next.note: Rates 'in all likelihood' need to rise, but how much and when is 'not a decision for right now'.

path.note: Hard to argue policy is restrictive enough while services inflation is sticky.

Fed|Daly.view: Inflation is a problem, mostly not from AI; firms are passing on costs; labour market stable.
Fed|Daly.shift: A usual dove now leaning to more hikes (since Nov 6).

next.note: Hike needed 'soon' (Oct 30) and several before spring 2027; no size named for December.

following.note: Several hikes needed before spring 2027 implies January or March too; not named.

path.note: The funds rate could be up to 100bp below where it needs to be.

Fed|Musalem.view: Policy still accommodative; risk of persistent above-target inflation outweighs the risk of tightening too early.
Fed|Musalem.shift: More hawkish: Oct 30 wanted a hike 'soon'; now sizes 100-150bp.

next.note: Calls for tighter policy and sees policy as accommodative; no meeting or size named.

following.note: Leans against an early-2027 pause; no meeting named.

path.note: Sees policy as fairly accommodative.

Fed|Schmid.view: Core inflation around 3% even without energy, so it can't be dismissed as a supply shock; the Fed has more work to do.

next.note: Additional tightening warranted 'soon'; asked about 50bp she stressed careful adjustment, implying 25bp.

following.note: Steady, gradual hikes; no meeting named.

path.note: Rates may have to rise more than expected.

Fed|Collins.view: Inflation too high and broadening; the inflation fight outweighs housing strains; risks on both sides.

next.note: Interim Atlanta Fed president; the Atlanta seat votes in 2027 (a permanent president is still being chosen).
Inflation will stay high over the coming quarters but she sees little reason to change course; no commitment on December (Nov 7-9).

following.note: Leaving the ECB early; may have gone by the February meeting.

ECB|Lagarde.view: Inflation set to stay high for some quarters; second-round effects no bigger than the ECB expected.

next.note: December hike looks 'very likely' (Nov 18); 25bp is the ECB's usual step.

path.note: Market bets on further tightening next year 'don't seem unreasonable' (Nov 16).

ECB|Vujcic.view: Energy prices and the Iran war keep pushing inflation up.

next.note: A December hike is prudent if the data don't shift (Nov 10-11); conditional.

following.note: Sets a very high bar for directional guidance; depends on wage and price spillovers.

ECB|Lane.view: Underlying inflation may rise even as energy prices fall; how far inflation spreads decides the path.
ECB|Lane.shift: More hawkish: Nov 6 was only 'gathering data' for December.

next.note: No recent remark on the December decision.

ECB|Schnabel.view: Recent speeches on fiscal stress and non-banks: fiscal pressure must not hijack monetary policy.

next.note: No recent remarks on rates (speeches on the digital euro).
No recent remarks on rates.
A December hike looks 'rather obvious' (Nov 10); 'very likely necessary' (Nov 3).

following.note: Further tightening possible after December; another hike 'highly probable' (Nov 13-18).

path.note: Sees no wage-price spiral yet (Nov 18).

ECB|Nagel.view: Energy is pushing inflation up and the ECB is far from its target; German recovery stronger than forecast.

next.note: Further increases could prove necessary, calibrated gradually given higher bond yields (Oct 30).

ECB|Panetta.view: Inflation above target for an extended period, risks to the upside; warns of a wage-price spiral.
ECB|Panetta.shift: Was among the doves: Oct 22 stressed that higher yields brake growth; Oct 30 said more hikes may be needed.

next.note: No view given on December.

ECB|Moulin.view: Calls policy measured and most prices stable (Oct 30); banks can handle higher rates.

next.note: Calls the rates outlook highly complex; no direction on December (Nov 2).
A December hike is likely; further tightening necessary (Nov 12).

following.note: Judgements on further hikes are getting 'more nuanced' (Nov 10).

ECB|Kazaks.view: Policy must stop energy inflation spilling into wider prices.

next.note: A December hike is his central scenario (Nov 16).

path.note: Further tightening next year might be necessary as second-round effects begin to show.

ECB|Simkus.view: Sees early second-round effects in expectations and firms' pricing; 2027 inflation forecasts could go up.

next.note: Seriously considered voting for a hike in October and says upside risks remain; has not named December.
The ECB will have to hike if the situation does not improve soon (Oct 30): conditional.

ECB|Kocher.view: Must keep inflation from becoming entrenched; neither acting too early nor waiting idly works.

next.note: Sees a 'rather big chance' of a December hike (Nov 5).
No recent remarks on rates.
No recent remarks on rates.
No view given on December.

ECB|Santos Pereira.view: Mid-October: euro-area inflation is not spreading beyond energy.

next.note: No view given on December.

ECB|Sleijpen.view: No second-round effects yet, but elevated energy prices are a clear upside risk (Nov 3).

next.note: No recent remarks on rates.
No view given on December.

ECB|Dolenc.view: The energy shock is not yet turning into broader price pressure (Oct 30).

next.note: No view given on December.

ECB|Rehn.view: Growth and inflation outlook still very uncertain (Oct 30).

next.note: A second hike is 'more likely than not' if the war goes on (Nov 5); more hikes needed if the conflict lasts (Nov 18). Conditional on the war, which is continuing.

path.note: How long the Iran conflict lasts is the key to the rate path; more hikes needed if it lasts (Nov 18).

BoE|Bailey.view: Upside risks to inflation; the labour market is no longer loosening, though some slack remains.

next.note: Her last vote (Nov 5) was for 50bp, citing non-linear inflation risks and credibility. No remarks since, so this is her November vote carried forward, not a new call for December.

BoE|Mann.view: Sees non-linear inflation risks with CPI heading to about 4.9% by mid-2027, and a large inflation risk premium in gilts.
BoE|Mann.shift: Has long argued for 'activist' bigger moves over gradual steps; voted for 25bp hikes in July and September before 50bp in November.

next.note: One 25bp hike unlikely to be enough, more near-term tightening probably needed; sees a very low chance the war ends soon.

following.note: Later moves depend on evidence of persistence in pay and pricing.

path.note: Called the ~90bp of tightening priced by end-2027 'not outrageous'; rates probably rise further in 2027; 'we waited too long'.

BoE|Pill.view: Second-round wage effects from the energy shock are the main worry.
BoE|Pill.shift: More hawkish: Nov 6 said rates could hold or even fall if growth stalls; Nov 14 sees further rises into 2027.

next.note: Additional hikes will likely be required; tighten proactively. December not named.

following.note: Proactive tightening against sticky pay growth; no meeting named.

path.note: Raising too much and cutting later beats waiting too long.

BoE|Greene.view: Failing to control inflation is the bigger policy mistake; less slack than thought.

next.note: Likely case for a further near-term increase unless inflation pressure weakens (minutes, Nov 10 speech); told the Guardian she does not rule out December.

following.note: Later rates conditional on the economy and energy.

BoE|Lombardelli.view: Risk that persistent inflation crystallises; balance of risks to the upside; labour market in low gear.

next.note: Expects more tightening if energy prices stay high, but financial conditions are restrictive enough for now (Nov minutes).

BoE|Breeden.view: Second-round effects still limited, but energy could entrench inflation.

next.note: No commitment to further hikes; less confident disinflation will continue and sees second-round risks rising (Nov minutes).

BoE|Ramsden.shift: Has moved from his dovish record toward tightening.

next.note: Would need clear evidence of recovering pricing power and wage-price pressure before keeping rates high for longer.

BoE|Dhingra.view: Saw the November hike as insurance against stronger pass-through.

next.note: Called November a 'one-for-now' insurance hike, not the start of a cycle; next move could be up, down or sideways.

following.note: Depends on energy and the 2027 pay round.

next.note: There could be a need to raise the rate further, but the Bank will proceed carefully, one meeting at a time.

path.note: No predetermined path; the policy rate is still low enough not to restrain growth.

BoC|Macklem.view: Can no longer look through the energy shock; businesses plan to pass on more costs; CPI near 3.5% by year-end.

next.note: No recent remarks on rates.
Speaking Nov 18 in Edmonton on scenario analysis and risk management; not yet reviewed.
No recent remarks on rates.
No recent remarks on rates.
No recent remarks on rates.
Won't say what the SNB will do in December; would not hesitate to adjust policy if price stability were at risk.

path.note: Negative rates possible if needed, but the bar is higher (Nov 6).

SNB|Schlegel.view: Inflation pressure slightly higher than in June, but the rise is mostly energy with no significant second-round effects so far.

next.note: No new signal on rates (general speech Nov 10).
No recent remarks on rates.
